name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district (D+17 PVI) with incumbent Deborah Ross running
Ross holds a large financial advantage ($1.3M cash) with no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price Ross at ~94% to win
Republican challenger has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The district's D+17 lean, Ross's incumbency and financial dominance, and market pricing near 94% all point the same direction, with no polls or ratings suggesting any risk. The forecast stays at a roughly 24-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing the Republican challenger within single digits, or major outside spending against Ross, would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Deborah Ross, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Raleigh-area district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 17 points. She has raised nearly $1.7 million and holds more than $1.3 million on hand, while her Republican challenger, Eugene Douglass, shows no reported fundraising and no outside groups are spending in the race. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the picture rests on the district's fundamentals, Ross's incumbency and money edge, and prediction markets that price her chances at roughly 94 percent. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic win, with the only meaningful uncertainty being how low turnout or a wave environment could compress the margin.
